items.heading: The Most Common Planning Mistake
items.text: The most common planning mistake is borrowing a study-hour target from a full-time aspirant's routine. A working aspirant's week is structurally different, and the plan needs to be built for that reality from the start.

items.heading: A Study Plan Only Works
items.text: A study plan only works if it can absorb a bad week without collapsing. Here is a structure that holds up against real job demands, not just an ideal week.

items.heading: This Is Your First Serious
items.text: This is your first serious attempt and you have not yet tested how much focused time you can actually protect.

items.heading: Your Job Genuinely Allows 3
items.text: Your job genuinely allows 3-5 quality hours most weekdays, even if it takes negotiation to get there.

items.heading: Your Household Depends on This
items.text: Your household depends on this income, or a job gap would be hard to explain to future employers if the exam does not work out.

items.heading: You Have Not Yet Built
items.text: You have not yet built a real routine, quitting before proving you can study consistently just removes the income cushion without fixing the discipline problem.
